newsitem.title: USA: Sun sets $105 million savings, more output.
newsitem.headline: Sun sets $105 million savings, more output.

text.p: Sun Co Inc expects to save $105 million this year and intends to increase output at its Northeast Refineries division by 30,000 barrels a day of gasoline and distillate and 3,000 barrels a day of chemicals, chairman Robert Campbell Drosdick said in a statement.

The company said that it would save $50 million due to an improvement at its Philadelphia and West Hook refineries, $20 million from its Northeast Marketing division and $35 million from reconfiguring its Puerto Rico refinery to process only intermediate feedstocks.
"These initiatives support the strategy Sun put in place beginning last summer to improve the company's financial performance," said Campbell.
Sun operates five domestic refineries with 777,000 barrels per day of crude oil processing capacity and markets gasoline via 4,000 service stations.

The completion of a polypropylene splitter project which came onstream in fourth quarter 1996 enabled it to upgrade 4,000 barrels of refinery grade polypropylene to chemical grade, said chief operating officer and company president Jack Drosdick.
Sun's stock closed up 3/8 at 26-5/8 prior to the release of the Sun statement.

Average daily production of gasoline in the northeast U.S. is 850,000 barrels and Tosco Corp recently announced that it will start up the Marcus Hook refinery in Pennsylvania later this year, which will add 70-80,000 barrels per day to the region's output.
